intent: K3: settle T-0144's unsanctioned org edits the way the operator ruled on 2026-09-12 (Q-010, register entry org-01a). ADR-0011 ratifies the four protected path lines the C7 codemod rewrote, because reverting them would take the auth-surface signal off the two files that carry it and re-edit two immutable ADRs to reinsert paths that no longer exist. The 47 closed records it also rewrote are restored to their pre-cdf95b10 text, because ADR-0010 section 3 says records are historical. A codemod is confined to its claims from here.

reasons.evidence: org/decisions/ADR-0011 is a new file in the protected set (org/policy.json:56). The operator's approval is on record as the Q-010 ruling of 2026-09-12, the oracle is authored by a session that is not the implementer, and the record carries a rollback plan.
47 restored files at 90 line pairs, plus the ADR

programme: K3 of the refactor and clean-up programme, executing the operator's ruling on Q-010 (governance as written).
invariants: I1 THE PROTECTED LINES ARE RATIFIED, NOT RE-EDITED. org/policy.json, ADR-0009 and ADR-0010 keep the paths the codemod wrote; ADR-0011 is the sanction and says so plainly, including that it is dated after the fact.

I2 A CLOSED RECORD SAYS WHAT WAS TRUE WHEN IT WAS WRITTEN. Every record closed before 2026-09-10 names no path C7 created. The oracle reads that property from the move map rather than from a list of files, so it keeps holding for every later move.
I3 THE RESTORE REVERSES THE CODEMOD AND NOTHING ELSE. It reverse-applies exactly cdf95b10's hunks, so anything a later batch legitimately changed in those files stays. Net zero lines.
I4 EIGHT FILES ARE KEPT, EACH NAMED WITH ITS REASON. The three protected files, the two inside T-0144's own claims, the one live record (T-0055), and the two living documents.
I5 THE ADR INDEX IS COMPLETE. docs/adr/README.md gains the missing ADR-0010 row beside the new ADR-0011 row (org-14).
rollback: Not one revert, which the first draft of this record claimed. git revert 9ae649e4 would restore the 47 files to their post-codemod text and remove ADR-0011, but that commit also carries the census baseline bump, the register correction, T-0150 and the ADR-0010 index row: the revert would leave the tree at todays test-line count against a baseline that no longer holds it, so census:lines exits 1, and it would strip the ADR-0010 row while ADR-0010 still exists, which turns the K3 oracle red. To roll back cleanly: revert 9ae649e4, then re-cut the baseline with a reason, then put back the ADR-0010 row. The ORACLE lane commits (661e4e3e, a634d89e) stand on their own and need not be reverted with it. No schema, no runtime code, no data.
commits: 013dcb0e the two lanes; 661e4e3e the K3 oracle, red at 4 of 8, by the ORACLE lane; f6ab7f94 the oracle lane also claims c8; a634d89e c8's testLines ratchet asserts the account, by the ORACLE lane; 9ae649e4 the ratification and the restore; 40f2d548 the mutants; the chore commit that carries this record and the views.
verification: Gate by the in-repo runner on the finished tree, stamp unmoved: lint 0 (54.6s), tsc 0 (3.5s), jest 0 (51.1s: 6951 tests, 688 suites), knip 0 (3.0s), canary 0 (0.7s), build 0 (25.4s), e2e 0 (137.8s), census 0 (49.8s), census:lines 0 (2.5s). The restore is 47 files, 90 insertions and 90 deletions, net zero, which is what a reverse-apply of one commit's hunks should be. The oracle went 4 of 8 red to 8 of 8 green. The first gate run stopped at jest on c8's testLines ratchet, which is recorded as a deviation below.
mutation: Three mutants against the committed tree at 40f2d548, all killed: a closed record rewritten again with the path the move created, the ADR-0010 row taken out of the public index, and a ratified protected line reverted to a path that no longer exists. The third is the batch's own argument, so it is the one worth having: the oracle sees the sensitive pattern stop resolving, which is why ratifying beat reverting.
deviation: Four. (1) The gate's first run stopped at jest: c8 held twelve measures at or below what C0 found, and this programme's oracles had taken testLines 116 lines past it. Every oracle a later batch writes would take it further, so it was put to the operator on its own and ruled the same day; a third ORACLE-lane amendment now asserts the growth account rather than a live count, and the census baseline keeps the live refusal. (2) The chosen option's wording, re-anchor to C8, does not survive the numbers: C8 left 121,114, which is stricter than C0's 121,762. The ORACLE session said so rather than implementing it, and the register's ruling line carries a dated correction. (3) That session also found the K3 oracle's 309 lines had landed in 661e4e3e without re-cutting the baseline, so census:lines was red at HEAD between the two commits; re-cut with its reason. (4) The oracle gates 43 of the 47 restored files. The four closed plans and reviews are not gated, because nothing in the tree separates a closed plan from a living one without a filename list, and a rule that fails a keep is worse than no rule. Named rather than faked; the cheap fix is a closed date in plan and review front matter.
